extracted.intended_audience: teachers, educators, and students of education
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for designing and applying teaching methods that integrate subject matter with instructional practice and foster reflective, purposeful learning. Emphasizes how general methods and individual methods interact and enumerates desirable intellectual traits in learners and teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essentials of method (five steps of reflective instruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: "They are first that the pupil have a genuine situation of experience--that there be a continuous activity in which he is interested for its own sake; secondly, that a genuine problem develop within this situation as a stimulus to thought; third, that he possess the information and make the observations needed to deal with it; fourth, that suggested solutions occur to him which he shall be responsible for developing in an orderly way; fifth, that he have opportunity and occasion to test his ideas by application, to make their meaning clear and to discover for himself their validity.", (summary of processes of instruction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use real, continuous activities that generate intrinsic interest; allow problems to emerge from the situation; ensure students have necessary information and observational experience; prompt students to generate and develop their own suggested solutions; provide occasions to apply and test ideas so students can verify meanings and validity. Anti-patterns: lessons that omit any of these steps (e.g., no genuine problem, no testing) weaken educative reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of subject matter and method
rubrics_metrics.description: "Method means that arrangement of subject matter which makes it most effective in use. Never is method something outside of the material."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat subject matter as a ready-made inert body separate from methods. Design method as an effective treatment of material directed to ends; organize subject matter so it both embodies and requires method. Avoid dualistic views that permit teaching 'methods' to be applied without regard to the character of the material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method as directed movement of subject matter toward ends (efficiency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Method is "the effective direction of subject matter to desired results"; efficiency = "such treatment as utilizes the material (puts it to a purpose) with a minimum of waste of time and energy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate methods by how economically and purposefully they use material to attain intended educational ends. Prefer approaches that minimize wasted time/energy and are well-adapted to the material rather than arbitrary procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive methods from observation of concrete situations of experience
rubrics_metrics.description: "There can be no discovery of a method without cases to be studied. The method is derived from observation of what actually happens, with a view to seeing that it happen better next time."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base method development on study of real instances of learning and teaching; collect comparisons of success and failure to identify causal conditions. Avoid prescribing authoritative methods divorced from observed classroom or life situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote cross-connections; avoid treating lessons as isolated wholes
rubrics_metrics.description: "The least desirable treats each lesson as an independent whole... Wiser teachers see to it that the student is systematically led to utilize his earlier lessons to help understand the present one, and also to use the present to throw additional light upon what has already been acquired."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design instruction so each lesson links to prior and future lessons and to out-of-school experiences. Habitually prompt students to find points of contact across subjects and contexts. Anti-pattern: teaching that leaves out-of-school experience crude and unrefined or presents each lesson in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject mechanical uniformity and rigid, prescribed steps
rubrics_metrics.description: "Under the influence of the conception of the separation of mind and material, method tends to be reduced to a cut and dried routine, to following mechanically prescribed steps... Nothing has brought pedagogical theory into greater disrepute than the belief that it is identified with handing out to teachers recipes and models to be followed in teaching."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage one-size-fits-all recipes and rigid formulas. Encourage teachers and students to experiment with methods, discriminate by consequences, and adapt approaches to particular cases. Recognize the danger that general methods can become mechanized and oppressive if treated as fixed rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance general methods and individual methods (adaptation)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Such matters as knowledge of the past, of current technique, of materials, of the ways in which one's own best results are assured, supply the material for what may be called general method... To be used intelligently, existing practices... have to be adapted to the exigencies of particular cases."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquire knowledge of established/general methods as intellectual aids, but adapt them to the unique needs of students and situations. Use general methods to suggest what to inquire and try, not as literal prescriptions. Evaluate a teacher by how well they integrate general knowledge with personal judgment and situational responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know materials and tools; study past practitioners' techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: "The painter must know canvas, pigments, brushes, and the technique of manipulation of all his appliances... The artist studies the progress of his own attempts to see what succeeds and what fails."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers should attain thorough acquaintance with subject-matter 'materials and tools' and established techniques. Study exemplars from the past and one's own practice to identify reliable procedures, yet remain ready to transform techniques for new uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual method traits – Directness (confidence, absence of self-consciousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Directness is characterized negatively: the absence of self-consciousness, embarrassment, and constraint; "Confidence... denotes the straightforwardness with which one goes at what he has to do... It signifies rising to the needs of the situation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster students' spontaneous, whole-souled relationship to subject matter; avoid instructional practices that make learners preoccupied with their own attitudes or with external impressions. Temporary reflective attention to method can be useful, but persistent self-consciousness undermines effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual method traits – Open-mindedness
rubrics_metrics.description: "Openness of mind means accessibility of mind to any and every consideration that will throw light upon the situation... An active desire to entertain considerations which modify existing purposes."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage intellectual hospitality: welcome alternate points of view and new information that may reshape purposes. Guard against excessive zeal for uniform procedure or quick measurable results that close off exploration. Open-mindedness is not passive; it requires active willingness to reconsider aims and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual method traits – Single-mindedness (whole‑heartedness, unity of purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-mindedness = "completeness of interest, unity of purpose; the absence of suppressed but effectual ulterior aims... Absorption, engrossment, full concern with subject matter for its own sake, nurture it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate wholehearted engagement with tasks and discourage divided attention, concealed ulterior aims, or motivation by external coercion/rewards. Avoid framing schoolwork as merely preparatory or dependent on extrinsic incentives, which breeds double-mindedness and superficiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual method traits – Responsibility and intellectual thoroughness
rubrics_metrics.description: "By responsibility... is meant the disposition to consider in advance the probable consequences of any projected step and deliberately to accept them... Intellectual thoroughness is seeing a thing through."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote habits of thinking that require students to follow implications of beliefs and to act on considered consequences. Prefer fewer deeply worked-out situations over congested superficial facts. Assess understanding by the extent to which students 'see through' meanings and are willing to accept practical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods should foster originality and avoid producing mediocrity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Imposing an alleged uniform general method upon everybody breeds mediocrity in all but the very exceptional... Ability to use even in a masterly way an established technique gives no warranty of artistic work, for the latter also depends upon an animating idea."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design instruction to enable individual initiative and originality rather than conformity to a single standardized method. Use general methods as resources to be transformed by personal insight; avoid measures that evaluate learners solely by conformity to standard procedures.
